       Detection of IgM antibody to Hepatitis A. A positive result indicates a current or recent hepatitis A virus infection. Anti-HAV IgM is usually

       detectable for 3 to 6 months after the onset of illness. The performance of this assay has not been established with cord blood, neonatal

       specimens, cadaver specimens, heat-inactivated samples or body fluids other than serum.

HEV (Hepatitis E Virus) Antibody, IgG (ID26A)

 

 

 

 

HEV (Hepatitis E Virus Antibody) - IgG

Sample : Serum   Methodology : Elisa

 

0.040

 

OD

< 0.9 ( Non Reactive)

0.9 - 1.1 (Borderline)

> 1.1 (Reactive)

 

 

 

 

 

      The HEV IgG antibody test detects IgG antibodies in the blood against Hepatitis E virus (HEV). These antibodies typically appear after the body

      has been exposed to the virus and are an indicator of past or resolved infection. The presence of IgG antibodies suggests that a person has

      previously been infected with HEV and may have developed immunity to the virus.

Sample : Serum   Methodology : Elisa

 

0.043

 

OD

< 0.9 ( Non Reactive)

0.9 - 1.1 (Borderline)

> 1.1 (Reactive)

 

 

 

 

 

      The HEV IgM antibody test is used to detect IgM antibodies specific to Hepatitis E virus (HEV) in the blood. IgM antibodies are produced early in

      response to an acute infection, making this test valuable for diagnosing recent or acute infections with HEV.
